name: Procurement Kickbacks and Bid Rigging
description: Improper payments or favours linked to public or private procurement, including kickbacks to buyers, inflated contract prices, bid rigging and phantom suppliers. Banks and corporates can detect patterns in supplier payments, related parties and post-award flows.

sources.text: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Public Procurement (2015)
OECD, Preventing Corruption in Public Procurement (2016)
OECD, Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement (2009)
FATF, Laundering the Proceeds of Corruption (2011)

exposure.rationale: Supplier payments and post-award flows to connected parties in procurement.

indicators.name: Contract price well above market or estimate
indicators.canon: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.desc: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
indicators.ctx: Awarded price materially exceeds engineers' estimates or comparable contracts without justification.
indicators.fp: Complexity, scope change and inflation can legitimately inflate prices.

indicators.name: Repeated wins by the same supplier with narrow margins
indicators.canon: Repeated wins by the same supplier with narrow margins
indicators.desc: One supplier repeatedly wins just below competitors or in rotation among a small group.
indicators.ctx: One supplier repeatedly wins just below competitors or in rotation among a small group.
indicators.fp: Niche markets may have few capable bidders.

indicators.name: Post-award payments from supplier to buyer-linked accounts
indicators.canon: Post-award payments from supplier to buyer-linked accounts
indicators.desc: Winning supplier transfers funds to persons or companies connected to the procuring official shortly after payment.
indicators.ctx: Winning supplier transfers funds to persons or companies connected to the procuring official shortly after payment.
indicators.fp: Supplier subcontracting may pay related parties innocently.

indicators.name: Supplier lacks capacity for awarded contract
indicators.canon: Supplier lacks capacity for awarded contract
indicators.desc: Awardee has no relevant staff, assets or experience and subcontracts nearly all work.
indicators.ctx: Awardee has no relevant staff, assets or experience and subcontracts nearly all work.
indicators.fp: Project vehicles are often newly formed and sub-contract widely.

indicators.name: Frequent contract variations or change orders
indicators.canon: Frequent contract variations or change orders
indicators.desc: Scope and price rise significantly through repeated amendments shortly after award.
indicators.ctx: Scope and price rise significantly through repeated amendments shortly after award.
indicators.fp: Genuine scope changes are common in construction and IT.

indicators.name: Emergency or single-source award with weak justification
indicators.canon: Emergency or single-source award with weak justification
indicators.desc: Use of urgency or sole-source exceptions for non-urgent purchases.
indicators.ctx: Use of urgency or sole-source exceptions for non-urgent purchases.
indicators.fp: Real emergencies exist and justify fast awards.

indicators.name: Phantom or fictitious supplier on vendor master
indicators.canon: Vendor linked to employee or without verifiable existence
indicators.desc: Vendor has no verifiable address, tax number or deliveries, or shares address or bank details with an employee.
indicators.ctx: Vendor with no verifiable address, tax number or deliveries shares details with an employee or another vendor.
indicators.fp: Data entry errors can create apparent duplicates.

indicators.name: Rapid bank account changes or payments to unrelated accounts for suppliers
indicators.canon: Payment directed to personal or third-party account
indicators.desc: Payment is requested to, or credited to, a personal, third-party or differently named account rather than the contracted payee.
indicators.ctx: Supplier asks to redirect payments to accounts held by third parties, often after award.
indicators.fp: Suppliers legitimately change banks or factor receivables.
